actual_tools: retained evidence from the GB1, PD-L1 assay, Boltz-2, and workflow-definition cases
execution.implementation: deterministic RO-Crate 1.1 directory and fixed-timestamp ZIP built from 16 existing case-specific evidence artifacts

observations: The RO-Crate inventory contains 16 selected artifacts from four source cases.
Validation reports zero missing files and zero content-size mismatches across 18 file entities.
The deterministic ZIP contains 20 members in lexicographic order with fixed timestamps.
A genuine Rosalind launcher call returned ready=true but did not copy files, build the RO-Crate, create the ZIP, or validate the export.
interpretation: The export makes heterogeneous source observations, computations, predictions, plans, and provenance easier to inspect and transfer.
Evidence classifications preserve the recorded scientific status of every included artifact.
limitations: Packaging does not increase the scientific strength of source evidence.
Large Boltz structure coordinates and the complete ProteinGym archive are represented through provenance rather than copied.
External source URLs can change after the recorded access date.
RO-Crate structural validation does not establish biological correctness.

provenance.note: The builder copies only existing selected artifacts, records their source paths and evidence classes, validates file presence and declared size, and writes a fixed-order archive. The Rosalind observation records chooser readiness only.

reproduction: Verify the four source case directories and run python build_case.py.
Inspect the inventory, JSON-LD metadata, validation report, and package guide.
Extract the ZIP into an empty directory and compare its member list with the RO-Crate directory.
